quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: More than half of all crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders with little experience.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Keep more distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam when other vehicles are not nearby, and keep extra distance behind other vehicles. Watch the headlights and taillights of vehicles ahead to see the road better.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection to:

options.text: See if parked vehicles are entering traffic.
Watch for vehicles behind you that are not slowing down.
See if someone is planning to turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for vehicles behind you that are not slowing down.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, use your mirrors to check for cars coming from behind. Drivers may not see you until they are very close, and you may need to react quickly.

questions.question: When being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.
Move back and forth across the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding too close to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding too far away may cause the other driver to merge back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: What reduces the effects of alcohol after drinking?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects on your body.

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Give you a clear view to both sides.
Block all air from passing through.
Be tight enough so glasses cannot fit underneath.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, give clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and have room for eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Keep more distance from the vehicle ahead.
Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow vehicles more closely.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, reduce your speed and keep extra distance from vehicles ahead. Use the lights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam, except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: A wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars may be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that do not work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Wobbles are usually caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make the problem worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not brake, as it may worsen the wobble.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Always press on the left handgrip.
Always press on the right handgrip.
Press on the handgrip opposite the direction you are turning.
Press on the handgrip in the direction you are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press on the handgrip in the direction you are turning.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Staggered lines are normally best, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:

options.text: The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If steering feels heavy, pull off the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds under 30 mph.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Use only mirrors to see other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let vehicles in blind spots pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is not usually dangerous. Just relax and go straight at a steady speed. Weaving to match the movement will only make it more dangerous.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: The best lane position:

options.text: Is always on the right side of the lane.
Is always in the center of the lane.
Is always on the left side of the lane.
Changes based on road, weather, and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on road, weather, and traffic.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on road conditions, weather, and traffic around you.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly over rough surfaces to keep control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: When another vehicle is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Let the other vehicle pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other vehicle pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may make them tailgate faster.

questions.question: When securing a load, place it:

options.text: On only one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Place loads as low as possible. High loads raise the center of gravity and affect balance. Distribute loads evenly on both sides to avoid pulling the motorcycle to one side.
